newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq drops as interest rates pressured stocks.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq drops as interest rates pressured stocks.

text.p: The Nasdaq Composite Index slipped slightly after two days of record highs as interest rates and profit-taking pressured stocks.

The Nasdaq Composite Index dropped 7.38 points to close unofficially at 1320.35. The Dow dropped 52 point to an unofficial close of 6549. In late trading, the long bond yield stood at 6.84 percent, its highest level in over two months.
"There's been some correction from the lofty levels seen the past two days," due to interest rates and profit-taking said Brett Discher, Dain Bosworth's vice president of equity trading.
Traders also said Federal Reserve Bank of New York President William McDonough's comments that U.S. stocks appeared fully valued also contributed to the selloff.
Technology stocks dropped Wednesday, with Netscape Communications Corp crumbling 10-7/8 to 47-7/8 after a Wall Street analyst lowered his rating.
Shiva Corp also plummeted 15-5/8 to 19-1/4 after several analysts cut their rating due to Shiva's fourth quarter earnings warning.
Gainers beat losers 2376 to 2009 on total volume of 683 million shares.
